raw_response:
I'm fifty this year, been farming these 3.5 mu for thirty years. Never went to school, can't read those books, but I know this land with my hands. Six of us in the house — my son and his wife work over at the garment factory in town, so it's mostly me and my old man in the fields, though the kids come back for harvest.

The corn just came off ten days ago. We got about 900 jin total, which is around 260 jin per mu — not great, the August heat was cruel and we only irrigated twice because the pump electricity cost too much. Now the stalks are cleared and I need to get the wheat in the ground before the middle of October. I always plant around October 8th, after the corn is threshed. Can't be late or the wheat won't survive the winter well.

For seed, I walk to Lao Zhang's shop and buy the same common wheat everyone grows — I don't know the name they write on the bag, but it's the yellow one. I sow about 30 jin per mu, so I need about 100 jin total for the whole plot. Costs me about 200-odd yuan. I save my own corn seed? No, can't do that with hybrid corn — I buy new hybrid seed every year for the summer crop, about 6 jin per mu.

Fertilizer is what keeps me up at night. Everything costs more now. For the wheat, I buy two big bags of compound fertilizer — the blue bag with the three numbers, I can't read them but I know the look. That's about 100 jin for the 3.5 mu. I spread it all before I plant. Then in spring, when the wheat starts growing fast around Qingming, I put down one bag of urea, about 50 jin for the whole field. The neighbor, Auntie Liu, told me her son said we should use more, but two bags of compound plus one of urea is already over 400 yuan, and we still have the corn season to pay for. Last year I used the same amount and got 420 jin per mu of wheat, so it should be fine.

Irrigation — the well water costs money. For wheat I usually water three times: once right after planting so the seeds set, once in March when it greens up, and once at jointing. If it rains good in April I might skip the last one, but last year was dry so I did all three. For corn, maybe one or two times, depending on the sky. The pump electricity for all these waters... every time I turn it on I see the meter spin and my heart spins with it.

For the corn, we'll plant right after the wheat harvest in early June. There's no time to rest — sometimes we cut wheat in the morning and plant corn in the afternoon. I put down one and a half bags of compound fertilizer for the corn, about 75 jin, and at the big trumpet stage I topdress with one bag of urea. If the leaves look yellow I might add a bit more, but urea is expensive.

Pesticides — I spray herbicide on the wheat once in early spring, and on the corn once after it comes up. If I see worms I'll buy some bug medicine from the shop, but last year there weren't many so I only spent about 30 yuan on that.

Labor is just us mostly. My old man and I can handle the planting and spraying. For the wheat harvest in June we might hire one person for a day to help carry, that's 150 yuan a day now. For the corn harvest we can manage ourselves.

I expect the wheat to give me about 400 jin per mu if the spring is decent, and the corn maybe 450 jin per mu if we get some rain. Last year the corn was lower, but you can't win every year. We need the wheat for our own flour, and the corn sells for cash or goes to the pigs. With fertilizer and seed and water and the hired hand, I'm looking at spending maybe 1,500 yuan total this year. That's a lot for us, but if I don't spend it, we get nothing.
